profile.summary: Preserve effective first VLA execution. When a real repeated mismatch is established, reuse a measured handle-hold or regrasp procedure with fresh inputs.
applicability: Atomic-only checkpoint 59999; native left/right drawer instruction remains active.
Development experience on seeds 0–9, not held-out evidence. All procedures remain candidates.

when: First VLA attempt or current phase still shows meaningful progress.
rules.rationale: Five original episodes succeeded without code recovery. Use brief running reviews; detailed recovery design belongs after a confirmed takeover.
avoid: Do not infer failure solely from a low reward or small EEF translation.

when: Current measured fingers and drawer geometry support an existing handle hold.
Repeated VLA execution has not produced outward drawer motion.
rules.rationale: Seed 5 succeeded with this controller family. The 0.30 m travel cap caused a redundant retry; a 0.45 m candidate completed its exact-prefix replay. Confirm current entry conditions; closure alone is insufficient.
avoid: Do not copy historical pixel boxes or observation_step.

when: Fresh evidence establishes open or missed grasp, requiring a whole-task recovery.
rules.rationale: Inspect drawer-regrasp-and-open entry variants and latest replay evidence before editing. Listed versions completed their development replay, not arbitrary new entries. Original episodes and replays exposed 3-pixel geometry below the 4-valid-pixel API minimum, persistent pose residual, fixed-window tracking loss and mixed U-shaped-handle geometry.
avoid: Do not rerun a known failed branch without addressing its measured failure.
Keep task_success and geometric validity checks; do not weaken completion to force a pass.

open_questions: Clearance, handle selection and tracking have only development-state tests; fresh entries may differ.
Replay evidence attached to skill versions is more recent than the original episode guidance.
